display.purpose: Hero/landing headlines only — login hero, empty-state welcome. Never used for UI chrome.

title.purpose: Page/section headings, e.g. "Sign in to Kompast".

body.purpose: The overwhelming majority of UI text — buttons, inputs, table cells, descriptions.

label.purpose: Badges, avatar initials, section overlines, and — in JetBrains Mono — issue keys, counts, timestamps, story points.

shadows.name: ambient-overlay
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system. Floating/overlay surfaces only: dropdowns, popovers, notification panel, version history. Dark theme: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.5), 0 10px 28px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.7).

motion.name: opacity-hover
motion.purpose: Default button hover — an opacity dip, never a color or position shift.

motion.name: sidebar-width
motion.purpose: Sidebar rail/tree collapse toggle — only animates on a user-triggered change, never on initial render.

motion.name: kp-blink
motion.purpose: Status/presence dot pulse (e.g. tenant-detected indicator on login).

motion.name: kp-rise
motion.value: @keyframes kp-rise { from { opacity:0; transform:translateY(6px) } to { opacity:1; transform:none } }
motion.purpose: Entrance animation for newly-appearing content blocks (e.g. AI-streamed responses).

components.name: Button — Primary
components.description: Highest-frequency call-to-action. Cobalt Focus fill, white semibold text.
components.css: .ds-btn { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:8px; border-radius:7px; font-size:13px; font-weight:500; padding:6px 12px; border:none; cursor:pointer; transition:opacity .15s; } .ds-btn:disabled { opacity:.5; pointer-events:none; } .ds-btn-primary { background:var(--accent,#2f6fea); color:#fff; font-weight:600; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity:.9; }

components.name: Button — Dark
components.description: The single highest-emphasis action per screen (e.g. "Continue with Microsoft").
components.css: .ds-btn-dark { background:var(--text,#191a1d); color:var(--bg,#f6f4ef); font-weight:600; border-radius:7px; font-size:14.5px; padding:14px 12px; border:none; cursor:pointer; transition:opacity .15s; } .ds-btn-dark:hover { opacity:.9; }

components.name: Button — Outline
components.description: Secondary action — hairline border, fills to the tertiary surface on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background:var(--surface,#fff); color:var(--text-2,#5b5d63); border:1px solid var(--border-2,#d3cec3); border-radius:7px; font-size:13px; font-weight:500; padding:6px 12px; cursor:pointer; transition:background .15s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background:var(--surface-3,#efece4); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--accent,#2f6fea); outline-offset:1px; }

components.name: Badge — Accent
components.description: Full-pill status/role tag. Six tones share this shape; only the color pair changes.
components.css: .ds-badge { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; border-radius:9999px; padding:2px 8px; font-size:10.5px; font-weight:600; } .ds-badge-accent { background:var(--accent-soft,#e8f0fe); color:var(--accent,#2f6fea); }

components.name: Avatar
components.description: Identity chip — reuses the badge tone system as a circle with bold initials instead of a pill with a label.
components.css: .ds-avatar { display:grid; place-items:center; width:22px; height:22px; border-radius:9999px; background:var(--violet-soft,#ebe7f6); color:var(--violet,#584a86); font-size:9.5px; font-weight:700; flex:none; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Primary container. No shadow at rest — a hairline border is the only separation.
components.css: .ds-card { background:var(--surface,#fff); border:1px solid var(--border,#e4e0d8); border-radius:12px; padding:16px; } .ds-card-title { font-size:15px; font-weight:600; color:var(--text,#191a1d); margin:0 0 4px; } .ds-card-body { font-size:13px; color:var(--text-2,#5b5d63); margin:0; font-family:'JetBrains Mono',monospace; }

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Underline tabs — a 2px bottom border is the only active-state signal. No pill or fill style.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display:flex; gap:2px; } .ds-tab { background:none; border:none; border-bottom:2px solid transparent; padding:8px 12px; font-size:13px; font-weight:500; color:var(--text-2,#5b5d63); cursor:pointer; transition:color .15s; } .ds-tab:hover { color:var(--text,#191a1d); } .ds-tab-active { border-bottom-color:var(--text,#191a1d); color:var(--text,#191a1d); font-weight:600; }

components.name: Compass Mark
components.description: The brand glyph — a rotated white diamond inside a rounded Cobalt Focus square. The one recurring icon the system treats as sacred; never a bitmap logo file in-app.
components.css: .ds-compass { display:grid; place-items:center; width:30px; height:30px; border-radius:9px; background:var(--accent,#2f6fea); } .ds-compass-diamond { width:8px; height:8px; border-radius:2px; background:#fff; transform:rotate(45deg); }

narrative.overview:
Kompast reads like a precise paper instrument, not a glossy SaaS dashboard: a warm, off-white ledger page (--bg) holds dense rows of small, exact type, with a single cobalt-blue mark — sampled straight from the compass logo — as the only loud color anywhere in the system. The compass mark itself (a rotated white square inside a rounded-square cobalt tile) recurs as the system's one recognizable shape; everything else is quiet geometry — hairline borders, small pills, a diamond of negative space — never an icon library.

The system is calm, precise, and unshowy on purpose. It explicitly rejects two easy defaults: it is not a playful, illustrated Notion clone, and it is not a loud, high-contrast dark-mode developer tool. Depth comes from borders and tonal surface steps, not shadow; personality comes from one restrained accent color and a serif/mono contrast in the type, not from decoration. A full dark theme exists ([data-theme="dark"]) as a disciplined token swap — same roles, same contrast relationships, inverted lightness — never a second, separately-art-directed look.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-paper neutral base with exactly one loud accent color (Cobalt Focus), used sparingly.
Editorial serif reserved for display headlines only; every other piece of text is small, sans-serif, and dense.
Mono, uppercase, wide-tracked type marks anything machine-scoped: issue keys, counts, timestamps, section overlines.
Flat by default — hairline borders separate surfaces; a single soft shadow token appears only on floating overlays.
No icon library. Every glyph (the compass mark, the blinking status dot, the Microsoft tile) is hand-drawn from primitive shapes.

rules.name: The One Loud Color Rule
rules.body: Cobalt Focus is the only saturated, attention-getting color in the system. Every other hue (indigo, green, amber, violet, danger) is muted and only ever appears in small doses — badges, avatar initials, status dots — never as a large fill.

rules.name: The Danger Independence Rule
rules.body: Danger/destructive red must never be derived from or share a value with the brand accent again — they were split apart deliberately so a rebrand of one can't accidentally soften the other.

rules.name: The Serif-Is-Rare Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif appears only on true display headlines (login hero, empty-state welcome). If a component needs emphasis anywhere else, reach for sans-serif weight/size, never the serif.

rules.name: The Mono Metadata Rule
rules.body: Any value that is machine-scoped rather than authored prose — an issue key, a count, a timestamp, story points, a section overline — renders in JetBrains Mono, small, and usually in Ink Mist. This is how the system visually distinguishes "data" from "content" without adding an icon or a label.

rules.name: The Overlay-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: If an element sits in normal document flow, it gets a border, not a shadow. Shadow is reserved for anything that visually floats above the page.

dos: Do keep Cobalt Focus rare — one primary action per view, not a wash of blue across the screen.
Do render machine-scoped values (keys, counts, timestamps, points) in JetBrains Mono per the Mono Metadata Rule, even in a brand-new component.
Do use a border for anything at rest and reserve shadow-kp strictly for floating overlays.
Do reuse the existing custom radius scale (7 / 9 / 10 / 12px / full) instead of Tailwind's stock rounded-md/rounded-lg defaults.
Do treat light/dark as one token swap — never author dark mode as a separately art-directed theme.
donts: Don't use Instrument Serif outside true display headlines — it must stay rare to keep its impact.
Don't add a shadow to anything resting in normal document flow (cards, sidebars, table rows) — that's the Overlay-Only Shadow Rule.
Don't pull in an icon library (Lucide, Heroicons, etc.) — every glyph in this system is hand-drawn from primitive shapes; an imported icon set would visually clash immediately.
Don't let the destructive/danger color drift back toward sharing a value with the brand accent.
